qs.q: A patient with a left-sided annular 'napkin-ring' colonic carcinoma presents with progressive change in bowel habit and clinical signs of bowel obstruction. Why do left-sided colorectal carcinomas typically present with obstructive symptoms earlier than right-sided lesions?
o: Left-sided tumours are exclusively adenocarcinomas driven by microsatellite instability
Bacterial flora in the left colon accelerate the production of mucosal ulceration and strictures
The right colon produces polypoid fungating masses that bleed occultly without narrowing the lumen
The left colon has a narrower lumen and the tumour grows as an annular constricting mass
qs.e: Left-sided colon cancers form annular napkin-ring lesions that easily obstruct the narrower lumen of the distal colon, whereas right-sided lesions have a wider lumen and present with occult bleeding and anaemia.

qs.q: A patient presents with acute abdominal pain. Which imaging modality is mandatory for every patient presenting with abdominal pain to rule out small bowel obstruction and perforation?
qs.e: Any patient presenting with abdominal pain must undergo a plain abdominal X-ray to rule out small bowel obstruction and perforation. CT scans are reserved for specific presentations rather than being required for every patient initially.

qs.q: Through what mechanism does gallstone ileus classically precipitate a small bowel obstruction?
o: A large primary stone grows inside the common bile duct
Bile duct inflammation causes strictures trapping gas
Calcium bilirubinate stones precipitate within the colon
A stone ulcerates into the duodenum and obstructs the ileum
qs.e: Gallstone ileus occurs when a stone ulcerates through the gallbladder directly into the duodenum and travels down to cause mechanical obstruction at the terminal ileum. It does not originate from primary stone growth inside the jejunum.

qs.q: A patient presents with symptoms of small bowel obstruction caused by a large gallstone that ulcerated through the gallbladder into the duodenum. Where does the obstruction typically occur?
qs.e: In gallstone ileus, the large stone typically causes obstruction at the terminal ileum after ulcerating through the gallbladder into the duodenum. The proximal small bowel is rarely the impaction site.
